findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed hot dogs and brats in the back cooler to be opened with no date mark. There is a system in place which automatically prints a date marking label when the package is opened. It seems these two packages were simply missed. PIC was informed and will educate staff on proper date marking. Ensure staff are placing date marking labels on packages after opening to prevent the sale of out-of-date products.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed no paper towels available for use at hand washing sink in back room. Towels were provided during inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:

(D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: 5-205.11  (Pf) Hand washing sink blocked by a cleaning brush and the mop bucket. Hand washing sinks must be accessible at all times. Reference 5-205.11. Mop bucket and brush werew removed from the hand sink and area in front of the hand sink. Do not block hand sink even though the sink rarely used.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11  (Pf) Liquid hand soap not provided at the hand washing sink in back room. Provide liquid soap at hand washing sink. Reference 6-301.11. Hand soap was provided to the sink in back room.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Foods stored in the walk in cooler read between 45°F and 50°F. Also Pico in the condiment cold holder is  45°F.  Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food (TCS) is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B). Do not store TCS foods in coolers that are unable to maintain them at safe internal temperature of 41°F or below. Call when repair is complete.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking is not on the foods in the walk in cooler including pico and various brats and hot dogs. Also Pico in the condiment cold holder is not date marked. This item may be turned over every 24 hours or sooner.  Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41°F  or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17. These foods were the same foods that were discarded due to temperature.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11  (Pf) Food establishment does not have food cooling equipment with adequate capacity for current operations. Provide equipment for cooling food, and holding cold food, that is sufficient in number and capacity to cool food rapidly to required temperatures within the required timeframes. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 4-301.11. The walk in cooler is being repaired as it is frozen according to the technician woking on it. Do not store TCS foods in the walk in unit until it is repaired and able to hold TCS foods safely.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on: 1) the counters between the soda machine and the cup holder, 2) in the soda machine drip tray especially around the tubes 3) the counters between the coffee pots and cap machine 4) . Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: Walk in cooler is holding food around 48F at time of inspection. The  units are being repaired and receiving  maintenance. The unit is designed with two sets of condensers to ideally keep food in temperature. The unit is divided by a make shift plastic corrugated. wall which does not allow the air to flow as designed. The HVAC person said that he would be done in an hour and have the units back on. A factor exasperating the situation is that the unit is divided in half by plastic walls installed by the company. These walls change the air flow of the unit. The air flow should be unrestricted so that in times like this the food in the south side of the cooler does not come out of temperature. Maintenance removed a section of wall and the air temperatures lowered approximately 5 degrees. It's not advised to restrict air flow unless the units are professionally structured to support this type of wall construction in the unit. Food was not discarded at this time. It should be back down to 41F or below in the next hour. If the food is above 41F for four hours or more it will be discarded. Some of the foods are being discarded by management. The condiment holder is holding food at 46F. Someone flipped the switch. The items were discarded. 750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.comment: Observed floors in the facility to be soiled with litter and debris primarily by the 3 part sink and counters in back. 750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors and maintain free of accumulated soil.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils

Discussed with manager better cleaning practices and storage/ quicker removal of wet rags. Will follow up in 3 weeks for progress.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained

Also observed several locations in the back room which appear to have had spills in the past that were not adequately cleaned. Discussed issues with the PIC and instructed to clean regularly.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.153 - Whipped topping in dispenser out at the service area was not marked with the time of preparation and was observed to have an internal temperature of 51F. Manager asked staff what time the product was prepared today; employee stated she thought it was from this morning. Whipped topping was removed from the service area and discarded.

When using time as a control, food shall be marked to indicate the time when product was removed from a temperature controlled environment. Properly label whipped topping, and do not leave the canister out past 4 hours at the food counter.

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Packets of urn cleaner were observed in the cabinet beneath the handsink at the food counter. Packets had varying degrees of water damage due to exposure to leaking waste water. Packets of urn cleaner were discarded during the inspection.

Food and equipment shall be protected from cross contamination at all times. Do not store food or any food related items, including single service articles/items, under the plumbing of any sinks.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - A) Tubes of creamer were not cut at an angle. Product was puddling in the tube. Creamer tubes were cut at an angle to eliminate puddling of product in the tubes.

B) Boxes of food were on the floor in the walkin freezer. A delivery was received late yesterday and had not yet been put away. Store food, regardless of packaging, up off the floor at least 6 inches.

Food shall be properly stored and protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750.830g - Quat test kits all had expiration dates in 2015, and when used to check the sanitizer concentration at the 3 part sink the strips registered at 200ppm. Inspector's instant change strips were showing a concentration of 400ppm. Manager stated new test strips would be purchased.

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.citation_text:
750.1130 - Bucket of moldy water was observed under the 3 part sink. No apparent leak was observed at the plumbing where the bucket was located. Moldy waste water was discarded in the mopsink during the inspection.

Liquid waste shall be disposed of as sewage and must be disposed of properly via the public sewage system.
NOTE: If buckets/containers are used to catch leaks from plumbing, etc. prior to repairs being made, the liquid waste must be disposed of as frequently as necessary to avoid molding of water and causing a nuisance/creating a potential food/water source for pests.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text:
750.1060 - Food counter handsink had a leak where the plumbing connected to the handsink basin. Maintenance worker was on-site during inspection and was made aware of the issue.

All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.comment:

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
Toxic items labeled and used properly

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.citation_text:
750.1160 - A soiled container was observed under the 3 part sink. When the container was removed from the area, dozens of small white insects (mold mites?) were observed in the moisture/debris that was present in the area. Manager cleaned under the 3 part sink and insects were no longer visible. Manager will place a call for service to Terminix as well.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - A) Several sandwiches (subs, deli sandwiches, breakfast sandwiches, chicken; BBQ pork, and cheese burgers) in the open face sandwich cooler had internal temperatures above 41F depending on location within the three tiered unit. Other sandwiches and potentially hazardous foods (PHF) in the unit were at proper temperature. The unit appeared to be working but for some reason was not holding consistent internal product temperatures throughout. All sandwiches from the bottom shelf and approximately half the sandwiches from the middle shelf (closest to the front edge) were voluntarily removed to be counted for waste and discarded (~50+ sandwiches). Manager called Corporate for service so necessary adjustments can be made to better hold all PHF at 41F/below throughout the unit. (see general comments).
B) Whipped cream in cold canister was at 50F at drink counter. Product was out for 4hrs at that point and was voluntarily discarded. (see general comments)
Maintain cold PHF at 41F/below at all times unless time control is used for a product (use/discard w/in 4hrs; product can't be placed back in cooler for later use).

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Spray bottle of liquid labeled Sani-T-10 tested at 0ppm quat. Manager noted that was an old bottle and should not be in use. Bottle was emptied and voluntarily discarded by Manager. Newer bottle of sanitizer solution test at proper concentration.
Maintain quat solutions at 200ppm. Check spray bottles daily and make new solutions as needed to maintain concentration at 200ppm.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text: 750.810 - Sanitizer solution for wiping cloths used to sanitize general surfaces did not test at 200ppm quat. Sanitizing solution was dispensing properly. Solution was murky/soiled from use and needed to be remade. Solution was remade and tested at proper concentration. Maintain sanitizer solution at 200ppm. Change solutions for wiping cloths every 2 to 4 hours or more often if solutions and wiping cloths become heavily soiled. (see general comments)

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.citation_text: 750.1120 - Handsink at drink/hotdog counter was being used to fill a pitcher with water. Manager and staff were advised on proper use of handsinks. Handsinks are to be accessible for handwashing at all times and used only for handwashing.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750.650a - Cutting board at 3 part sink had black discoloration and small nicks throughout on both sides. Replace the cutting board with one that can be easily maintained clean. Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text: 750.690 - A) Cover to cheese sauce dispenser is cracked/broken on the right side. Replace the damaged cover. B) Heavy ice buildup was observed in the ice cream freezer. De-frost the ice cream freezer. C) Shelves behind the door in the back storage room were damaged (rough particle board exposed). Repair or replace the damaged shelves. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text: 750.810 - Wet wiping cloth was observed on the edge of the front counter by cash register/check out. Store wiping cloths in sanitizer solution between uses to inhibit the growth of microorganisms. Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. ** If spray bottles of sanitizer are used, then disposable paper towels must be used and discarded after each use.**

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - Chopper used to dice foods appeared to have food debris stuck on chopping surfaces. Chopper was moved to 3 part sink by inspector. findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
